subject: Proposal: multi-window co-term + optional auto-renew — NexaHealth
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Claire O'Neill <claire.oneill@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: multi-window co-term + optional auto-renew — NexaHealth

Claire —

Thanks again for the time last week. As discussed, attached is a concise proposal that aligns NexaHealth's different BU contracts into a single co-termed structure while preserving a flexible ramp for the first 18 months and an optional auto-renew clause. High-level summary below: 

- Term: 36 months (co-terming all current agreements into single renewal date)
- Ramp: Year 1 = 40% of committed capacity (frontloaded credits applied), Year 2 = 70%, Year 3 = 100%
- Pricing: 10% blended discount vs list for the committed volume; overage rates tiered by usage
- Auto-renew: opt-in at the BU level with 60-day notice; customers may opt out with no penalty
- Credits: Up to 3 months of credits frontloaded to offset migration and onboarding costs

Attachments: 20260914_Karthik_Proposal_NexaHealth.pdf (proposal + pricing table), nexa_ramp_schedule_v2.xlsx (detailed ramp), sample DocuSign link in doc.

Next steps: If this looks directionally correct, can we align on (1) whether procurement needs a separate SOW for onboarding credits and (2) target date for legal to review the amendment? Happy to run through the numbers with Rajesh if helpful.

Cheers,
Karthik
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

---
Karthik Iyer
Redwood Inference

From: Claire O'Neill <claire.oneill@nexahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Gupta <rgupta@nexahealth.com>, procurement@nexahealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:14 -0400
Subject: Re: Proposal: multi-window co-term + optional auto-renew — NexaHealth

Karthik —

Thanks for the proposal and the clear summary. A few quick procurement questions so we can move this internally: 

1) For the frontloaded credits, are those applied as invoice credits or as usage credit (i.e., reduces token consumption first)? We need to align with our finance recognition.
2) Does the 10% blended discount assume all BUs are consolidated under the same SLO/region? We have one BU that will remain in eu-west for latency requirements.
3) Can you provide a short version of the ramp schedule that we can attach to our PO (one page)?

I attached a short procurement checklist with the items the team typically returns to vendors (nexa_procurement_questions.docx). If you can answer inline, that will speed things up.

Also, legal will want to see the amendment language around auto-renew and the opt-out flow.

Best,
Claire O'Neill
Head of Platform Partnerships | NexaHealth
claire.oneill@nexahealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: multi-window co-term + optional auto-renew — NexaHealth

Claire / Rajesh —

Appreciate the quick feedback and excellent questions — answers below inline and I've attached a one-page ramp summary as requested.

1) Credits: The frontloaded credits are issued as invoice credits applied against billed usage until exhausted (they act as a reduction to your invoice line-items). If you need credits that reduce token burn accounting directly we can map to a usage-credit workflow but that requires a short SOW change (we've captured both options in the attachment).

2) Regions: The 10% blended discount assumes consolidation onto our verified model variants; for the eu-west BU we can keep region-specific routing and exclude it from the blended calculation, or we can include it at a 5% uplift depending on capacity commitments. I've added a regional carve-out row in the pricing table.

3) One-pager: attached as "nexa_ramp_summary_onepager.pdf" (also included inside 20260914_Karthik_Proposal_NexaHealth.pdf).

Internal note: copying Lauren to confirm if we should hold the 10% discount as final or propose a 7.5% starting discount with an acceleration clause tied to year-over-year usage growth.

Next steps: If procurement is happy with invoice-credit treatment and the regional carve-out, we can route a single amendment + SOW to legal and push to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: multi-window co-term + optional auto-renew — NexaHealth

Team — forwarding Claire's procurement questions and my responses. Quick ask: procurement is likely to accept invoice-credit treatment but will push for the eu-west BU carve-out not to be in the blended discount. They also asked for a short one-pager they can attach to their PO.

Proposal for approval: 
- Offer 3-year co-term with 10% blended discount if we include all BUs (including eu-west). If they insist on a carve-out for eu-west, drop to 7.5% blended but keep the frontloaded credits.
- Frontloaded credits = 3 months invoice-credit applied first to billed usage; no changes to recognition on our side.

Can you confirm margin/discount approval and whether I should keep the blended 10% or move to the contingency 7.5%? If approved, I'll instruct legal to prepare a single amendment + SOW and route for DocuSign.

Thanks — Karthik

Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposal: multi-window co-term + optional auto-renew — NexaHealth

Karthik / team —

Thanks for the heads up. Approve the contingency approach: lead with 10% blended (full consolidation) in the commercial proposal but be prepared to accept 7.5% if NexaHealth insists on a regional carve-out. Keep the 3 months frontloaded invoice-credit (good attenuation for migration risk).

A couple of operational asks before you send to legal: 
- Add a clause in the SOW that the frontloaded credits expire 12 months after signature if unused (prevents indefinite credit liability).
- Auto-renew opt-in must require explicit BU-level acceptance and a 60-day pre-notice; include an early-exit right for the first 6 months for the eu-west BU if they want to trial initially.

Once legal confirms the amendment language, push it to DocuSign and request countersignature within 10 business days.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
